volatility.description: The source-visible series make their largest jumps in HBM3E/HBM4E/HBM5.

narrative.headMessage: HBM generations lift capacity and bandwidth
narrative.subMessage: Bars show how much can be stored; the line shows how fast it moves. Both rise toward HBM5.
narrative.headline: HBM generations lift capacity and bandwidth
narrative.summary: The chart shows, in one view, how much memory an HBM generation can hold and how quickly it can move data.
narrative.story: A larger warehouse is not enough if the door is still narrow. AI needs both more room and a faster path in and out. Here, bars are maximum capacity and the line is bandwidth; both rise sharply in the newer generations.
keyTakeaways: HBM4E and HBM5 reach the highest visible capacity bars at about 64GB.
The bandwidth line rises from about 3TB/s after HBM4 to above 6TB/s at HBM5.
The values are source-visible readings, not a raw-data claim.
narrative.viewerAction: Read the bars and line against their own axes; the units are different.
contextualNotes: Samsung · HBM Development History · Hot Chips 2026
Point labels are not printed in the source image.

focusPoint.reason: The highest visible bandwidth point and 64GB bar show the latest-generation step-up.
